paper.title_en: Reconfigurable Dysprosium Isotope Mixtures with Selectable Quantum Statistics
paper.abstract_en: Dipolar quantum mixtures offer new opportunities to explore many-body phenomena shaped by long-range anisotropic interactions, intercomponent coupling, and quantum statistics. Here we develop a reconfigurable platform for bosonic and fermionic dysprosium isotope mixtures using a single-isotope-like optical layout. We time-multiplex the 421-nm light to generate isotope-selective slow-atom fluxes, while spectrally engineered 626-nm light provides simultaneous common-path narrow-line cooling and trapping. By reconfiguring optical frequencies, we prepare seven isotope pairs spanning Bose--Bose, Bose--Fermi, and Fermi--Fermi combinations, with continuous population-balance control through the 421-nm dwell-time allocation. Systematic comparisons with sequence-matched single-isotope references, from magneto-optical-trap loading and compression to optical-dipole-trap transfer, reveal nearly single-isotope-like performance for most combinations. The larger deviations occur only for certain isotope pairs and preparation stages, with controlled measurements revealing optical sensitivities during loading and additional losses under high-density conditions. Our results make isotope composition and quantum statistics selectable within a strongly dipolar system while largely preserving single-isotope preparation simplicity and performance, opening new possibilities for exploring multicomponent dipolar quantum matter.
